source.title: Supervised Contrastive Representation Learning: Landscape Analysis with Unconstrained Features

record.file_problem: Full paper text is supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes whether local optima are global for supervised contrastive loss in an unconstrained-features proxy, bearing conceptually on whether optimization encounters bad minima. It is a theoretical analysis rather than a test of the stated benchmark training recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper gives theoretical results for the UFM and cites prior empirical benchmark studies, but reports no new benchmark training outcomes. Rows below capture its own stated theorem results; cited empirical reports are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves landscape and embedding-geometry results for free feature vectors under supervised contrastive loss. It does not test any stated version. In particular, its feature-dimension condition does not measure gradient-descent success or extra student neurons in V2's two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but omits the standing sufficient temperature condition. Under that condition and d > k, the authors prove that every local minimum of the relaxed, norm-bounded supervised-contrastive UFM is global and that optimal geometry is unique up to rotation. They derive a reduced characterization for STEP-imbalanced data and recover ETF geometry for balanced data. Optimization dynamics and general-distribution geometry remain future work; eventual gradient-descent convergence is conjectured rather than proved.
record.recipe_differences: The study proves properties of an unconstrained-features proxy with full-batch supervised contrastive loss; it does not run the benchmark gradient-training recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The neural-collapse result is stated under a sufficient temperature condition; the global-optimality theorem assumes feature dimension d > k. The paper also distinguishes balanced from imbalanced data geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: Under d > k and the standing sufficient temperature condition, every local minimum of the relaxed supervised-contrastive UFM is global.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The norm-bounded supervised-contrastive free-embedding problem has no spurious local minima under these assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Global minimizers share one Gram matrix; balanced-data optimal class embeddings form a simplex ETF.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The studied supervised-contrastive UFM has unique optimal geometry up to rotation, with ETF geometry for balanced classes.

fits_no_version.finding: Every local minimum exhibits identical embeddings within each class under the sufficient temperature condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-class neural collapse holds at local minima of the norm-bounded supervised-contrastive UFM under the stated temperature condition.

record.problems: The analysis uses the UFM proxy and focuses on full-batch loss; it does not measure gradient dynamics or benchmark classification error. The neural-collapse lemma requires a sufficient temperature condition, and the authors leave general training distributions and optimization dynamics for future work.
record.rows_left_out: R5 is omitted because its statement is explicitly attributed to cited work [22], not reported as a new result of this study. Prior benchmark convergence reports discussed in the paper are also cited findings, not this study's results.

untested.parts: Training classification error of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels, model size and training-recipe conditions.
Gradient-descent outcomes in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization and normalization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent learning speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature dynamics, recovery and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The cannot_determine states refer to the supplied claim versions, not to whether the paper states its theoretical results. No version-specific verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR benchmarks, random or corrupted labels, model-size sweeps, or SGD/Adam training outcomes are reported.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or neuron-width sweep is studied.
No depth, shortcut, normalization, or training-error comparison for deep networks is tested.
No initialization comparison or trainable-depth experiment is conducted.
No learning-rate or sharpness dynamics are tested.
No batch-normalization comparison or training-speed measurement is conducted.

rows.value: All local solutions are global optima.
rows.note: Analytical theorem for the unconstrained-features model, not an empirical gradient-training or classification-error result.
rows.check: The theorem establishes the stated proxy-model result, but cannot establish any claim version. Add the standing assumption τ > 2/log((n−1)/(nmax−1)), explicitly imposed after Lemma 1. The variables are free embeddings with squared norms bounded by 1/τ, rather than a trained toy network.

rows.note: The result concerns embedding geometry, not training classification error.
rows.check: Gram-matrix uniqueness does not measure any version's effect. Add the standing temperature assumption used throughout the remaining results. The subject is a free-embedding optimization problem.
